label: no
controls_available: Full-mode pointer drag on the visible Poincare-disc canvas applies a Mobius translation to pan the view; it records a view-only pan event and does not mutate sticker state.

A full-mode canvas click on a visible heptagon twists it when the transformed face center is inside the central activation aperture: left click is counter-clockwise and right click is clockwise. Each accepted twist mutates the sticker state and consumes one of the four twists.
RESET SCRAMBLE restores the generated scramble and clears the view and event transcript; CERTIFY submits the replay, and FRESH CHALLENGE is available after failure.
autonomous_processes: None. Between pointer or button events the puzzle state, Mobius view, twist count, and action availability remain unchanged; the runtime defines no task timer, animation, physics, or autonomous random progression.
grouped_control_modes: D1: all full-mode Mobius pan drags across seeds, rounds, and attempts; these change only the visible view.
D2: all full-mode canvas twist clicks across seeds, rounds, and attempts, grouped over face, button direction, and current view; these are the outcome-affecting sticker-state actions.

clause_i.reason: For D2, the first optimal face and direction vary with the generated two-twist scramble. At the same initial action history, an action-history-only q cannot select the seed-dependent visible face and button direction; a screenshot can supply that information. This static state-dependence is not sufficient for real-time classification.

clause_ii.reason: A zero-length bounded window containing the current screenshot is sufficient in principle: the colored heptagon stickers, face geometry, and central aperture are visible, so a stationary visual policy can choose the next full-mode click. No consecutive-frame observation is required.

clause_iii.reason: For every legitimate D and every Delta > 0, supplying no new action leaves the rendered puzzle and its sticker state unchanged. The pan and twist controls do not become unavailable or less effective merely because task time passes; the only configured time limit is a deadline, which cannot supply the required non-clock task-state loss. Thus no available action has the required strict Q loss before the next action.

common_visible_process: No common visible autonomous process exists. All relevant changes are caused synchronously by pointer/button handlers: pan changes the view and twist changes stickers; idle rendering is static.

pre_run.reason: The configuration already fails the mathematical definition on clause (iii), so the pre-run override cannot change the No label. There is no autonomous outcome phase to start: after preparation, the puzzle waits for outcome-affecting pointer input.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 is configured as face_count 10, scramble_length 2, and move_budget 4; full interaction uses a Mobius drag plus left/right click twisting, with observation_window_ms 0 and one frame.
The generator reads the supplied difficulty parameters, builds the static puzzle geometry and twist cycles, sets activation_radius to 0.30, and emits the initial sticker state and move budget.

The seed changes rotation, palette, scramble faces, and directions; the recorded solution is the reverse inverse of that scramble, so the required next twist depends on the visible generated state rather than an action clock.
Sticker mutations occur only inside applyTwist, which is reached by pointer handlers; full mode accepts canvas pointer drags for Mobius view changes and no-motion left/right canvas clicks for twists.
Reset and submission are explicit event handlers, and rendering installs event listeners without any timer, animation loop, or autonomous state-update path.
The complete mechanic stylesheet supplies static layout, hover styling, cursor styling, and a media query; it defines no CSS animation or keyframe task process.
The grader maps full interaction to canvas_click and replays only pan/twist events, checking geometry, permutations, and the four-move budget without any elapsed-time or autonomous-state condition.
The export verifier independently replays the same input transcript and validates the final solved state and twist count; it has no task-time evolution check.

The scripted solver immediately focuses and turns each recorded solution face, then certifies; its waits are only for synchronous UI event completion and it contains no timed or motion-following control.

The frozen definition requires one visible autonomous process that makes an action strictly worse within Delta; a deadline or a static puzzle without non-clock state loss does not satisfy clause (iii), and the pre-run override applies only after the mathematical test.
